newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila suspends VMC debt payments.
newsitem.headline: Manila suspends VMC debt payments.

text.p: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) ordered on Tuesday the suspension of debt payments by cash-strapped Victorias Milling Corp (VMC) totalling 5.07 billion pesos.
Victorias had petitioned the SEC to shield it from its creditors after negotiations with them in the past several weeks bogged down.

"All actions or claims against Victorias pending before any court, tribunal, office, board, body and or commission are deemed suspended immediately until further order," the SEC said in a six-page order, a copy of which was released to reporters.
But the SEC ordered the sugar miller from disposing any of its properties.
The SEC also has to decide whether it would form a committee to rehabilitate Victorias.
Victorias said it has total assets of 7.1 billion pesos as against total liabilities of 5.07 billion.
On June 24, the SEC also suspended debt payments of Victorias' trading arm North Negros Marketing Corp.
Both Victorias and North Negros blame their financial woes to the slump in the local sugar industry due to increasing competition from cheaper imports.
